The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) has announced a new Aadhaar mobile application for iOS and Android devices. The authority has announced an early access that will allow residents to test the service and share feedback before its final rollout.

As per the announcement, the app is available on the Google Play Store and Apple App Store, offering users a digital option to carry their Aadhaar and use it for instant verification. The new app enables residents to use Aadhaar digitally without relying on physical documents. While the government continues to issue physical Aadhaar cards, the digital copy helps streamline verification for banking, admissions, driving licences, passports and other services.

UIDAI New Aadhaar App Key Features

Users can share their Aadhaar digitally, removing the need for physical copies.

Aadhaar details can be shared using a QR code or as verifiable credentials.

Shared Aadhaar data is masked, so users do not reveal the full 12-digit number.

Up to five Aadhaar profiles can be added on one device if they are linked to the same registered mobile number.

The feature supports parents who manage their children's Aadhaar profiles on their number.

The app includes biometric locking and unlocking.

Once locked, biometric data remains secure until it is intentionally unlocked or disabled.

The standard height for a basketball hoop (the top of the rim) is exactly 10 feet (3.05 meters) above the floor.

This measurement has remained the standard since the game was invented by Dr. James Naismith in 1891.

Whether in the NBA, FIBA, or NCAA, this height is uniform for all professional and high-level competitive play.

Other Measurements:

The backboard typically measures 6 feet (1.83 m) wide by 3.5 feet (1.07 m) tall.

The inner diameter of the rim is 18 inches (45.72 cm).

The three-point line distance varies (e.g., 23.75 ft in the NBA vs. 22.15 ft in FIBA), but the hoop height never changes.

The Global Innovation Index (GII) ranks 139 world economies according to their innovation capabilities. In its 18th edition, India ranks 38th overall, from 39th last year, and a 10-place jump from 2020 (48).

The country leads the pack among the 37 lower middle-income group economies and also ranks first among the 10 economies in Central and Southern Asia.

Strong policy support, growing R&D investment, and a vibrant startup ecosystem have propelled India's rise as a global innovation hub.

Consisting of roughly 80 indicators, grouped into innovation inputs and outputs, the GII aims to capture the multi-dimensional facets of innovation.

India performed better in innovation outputs than innovation inputs in 2025. The country's R&D investments fell to 7.8% in 2019-20, However, in the decade (2010-20) it rose 3.1%.

India's technology adoption ' fuelled by robust digital infrastructure, AI uptake, and government initiatives ' has propelled it to 39th place, a significant leap from 81st in 2015.

The Wanchos are a tribal community inhabiting the south-western Tirap District of Arunachal Pradesh. Their primary livelihood is jhum (shifting) cultivation, and their society is governed by a chieftaincy system with the Ngowang as the village council. They believe in one omnipotent God called Jowan Rang (God in the sky) and follow a code of living called vaanlam.

Oriah is the most important festival of the Wanchos - an agricultural festival celebrated at the beginning of spring, after the completion of jhum preparatory work like jungle clearing, burning, and sowing. The word itself breaks into 'O' (sacred offering and prayers) and 'Riah' (leisure and celebration). Dates vary by village according to their lunar calendar, announced by the Ngowang council.

The defining symbol of Oriah is the Zangvaan - a sacred bamboo post with seven branches erected at a platform called the Zangvaan Tong. Offerings of rice beer (Ju), cattle, and pigs are made to Jowan, with prayers for good harvest, health, and prosperity.

At Longding, Oriah has been celebrated every 16th February since 1975, with the broader purpose of unifying all Wancho villages, healing past inter-village feuds, and preserving ancestral culture. Modern additions like community feasts, cultural programmes, and literary competitions have been incorporated, while the core spirit of the festival remains intact.

· The correct statement about Gross National Product (GNP) is that it includes net factor income from abroad (NFIA).

· GNP measures the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced by the residents of a country, regardless of whether the production takes place within the domestic territory or abroad.

· The formula is: GNP = GDP + NFIA.

· NFIA is the difference between factor income earned by residents from abroad and factor income paid to non-residents working in the domestic territory.

Explanation of Other Options:

· It excludes consumption of fixed capital: This is incorrect. "Gross" in GNP means it includes the consumption of fixed capital (depreciation). Net National Product (NNP) excludes depreciation (NNP = GNP - Depreciation).

· It only measures production within domestic territory: This describes Gross Domestic Product (GDP). GNP includes income from abroad.

· It does not account for depreciation: This is misleading. "Gross" means depreciation is included. If depreciation were "accounted for" by subtracting it, it would become Net National Product.

Further insights:

· GNP provides a measure of the economic well-being of the residents of a country.

· If NFIA is positive (residents earn more from abroad than non-residents earn domestically), GNP will be greater than GDP. If NFIA is negative, GNP will be less than GDP.

A number divisible by 16, 27 and 35 must be divisible by their least common multiple.

Let A = required value to be added.

Least common multiple of 16, 27 and 35

16 = 24

27 = 33

35 = 5 X 7

LCM = 24 X 33 X 5 X 7

LCM = 15120

45189 ÷ 15120 gives remainder 14949

Least value to be added

A = 15120 − 14949

A = 171

By the composite rule of divisibility, given number is also divisible by 9 and 2.

To be divisible by 9, sum of digits of the given number should be divisible by 9.

questions.question: Choose the most suitable option to replace the bold part of the sentence. If the sentence is already correct, select 'No improvement'. As soon as the mountain weather station transmits the revised coordinates, the rescue pilot had altered the descent path accordingly.
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the bold part of the sentence. If the sentence is already correct, select 'No improvement'.

As soon as the mountain weather station transmits the revised coordinates, the rescue pilot had altered the descent path accordingly.
questions.solution:
The alteration of the descent path will happen after the station transmits the revised coordinates, so WILL ALTER is the correct choice. The clause introduced by "as soon as" takes simple present for the future trigger, while the main clause takes future simple for the later action. Rule-based deduction: English says, "As soon as he calls, I will leave," not "I had left."

• Option (a): ALTERS gives a simple present form, which does not clearly express the later future action intended here.

• Option (b): WILL HAVE ALTERED suggests that the alteration will already be complete before the coordinates are transmitted, which is illogical in this context.

• Option (c): WILL ALTER is correct because it shows the main future action after the trigger.

• Option (d): No improvement is incorrect because HAD ALTERED is a past perfect form and does not fit the future sequence.

questions.question: The figure of speech used in "The angry storm pounded on the door of the village"?
questions.questionHtml: The figure of speech used in "The angry storm pounded on the door of the village"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option c) Personification.

Personification is a figure of speech where human qualities, emotions, actions, or characteristics are given to inanimate objects, animals, or abstract ideas.

The sentence gives the storm (an inanimate natural event) two human attributes:

The emotion of being "angry."

The physical action of "pounding," as if it had fists.

This makes the storm seem like a living, menacing creature with a will of its own, creating a more vivid and threatening image for the reader.

A metaphor is a figure of speech that makes a direct comparison between two unlike things by stating that one thing is another. It does not use "like" or "as." The sentence does not say the storm is something else. It describes what the storm is doing in human terms.

A simile is a figure of speech that compares two unlike things using the words "like" or "as." The sentence does not use "like" or "as" to make a comparison.

Hyperbole is an extreme and deliberate exaggeration used for emphasis or humorous effect. It is not meant to be taken literally. While the phrase "pounded on the door of the village" is figurative, its primary function isn't exaggeration. The core literary device is attributing human action (pounding) and emotion (anger) to the storm. The phrase isn't exaggerating a quantity or quality to an impossible degree.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The given sentence contains an infinitive phrase ('to do') following the structure 'There is...'.

The format in Active voice is: There is/are + Noun + to + V1.

The format in Passive voice is: There is/are + Noun + to be + V3.

For example:

There is no time to lose. (Active)

There is no time to be lost. (Passive)

Option (c) correctly changes 'to do' to 'to be done' while also correctly passivizing the second clause [conversion of "we can finally launch the new product" to "the new product can be finally launched by us"].

The options except (c) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (c): There is a lot of work to be done before the new product can be finally launched by us in the international market.

Note: V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

questions.solution:
The first part of the sentence in the Direct Speech is in Present Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Past Continuous Tense.

Present Continuous (Subject + is/am/are + V1 + ing + Object) should be converted into Past Continuous (Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object).

For example:

He said, "I am checking the assignment." (Direct Speech)

He said that he was checking the assignment. (Indirect Speech)

The second part of the sentence in the Direct Speech is in Present Simple Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Past Simple Tense.

Present Simple (Subject + V1/V5 + Object) should be converted into Past Simple (Subject + V2 + Object).

For example:

He said, "I check the assignments." (Direct Speech)

He said that he checked the assignments. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

"I" changes to "he".

"am feeling" changes to "was feeling".

"think" [Present Indefinite in direct speech] changes to "thought" [Past Indefinite in indirect speech].

"need" [Present Indefinite in direct speech] changes to "needed" [Past Indefinite in indirect speech].

Therefore, the correct answer is: "My cousin whispered to me during the ceremony that he was feeling a bit unwell and he thought he needed some fresh air."

Hence, option (d) is correct.

Note: V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

questions.questionHtml:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence.

A. Despite the numerous challenges posed by climate change, various international agreements have been formulated to address its adverse effects on the planet's ecosystems.

B. These agreements emphasize cooperation among nations to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and promote sustainable development practices.

C. Climate change, caused primarily by human activities such as fossil fuel combustion and deforestation, has led to severe weather anomalies, melting ice caps, and rising sea levels.

D. The success of such accords, however, depends largely on the willingness of individual countries to implement policies and meet emission targets effectively.
questions.solution:
The correct sequence is CABD.

Sentence C introduces the problem by describing the causes and consequences of climate change.

Sentence A follows by mentioning the international efforts to combat these problems, setting the stage for global action.

Sentence B elaborates on the nature of these agreements, focusing on cooperation and goals.

Sentence D logically concludes by explaining the condition for success, highlighting the role of individual nations. This order moves from problem to solution to cooperation to implementation challenges.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Despite facing repeated setbacks in her research, Dr. Mehra remained ________ in her pursuit of a breakthrough.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Despite facing repeated setbacks in her research, Dr. Mehra remained ________ in her pursuit of a breakthrough.
questions.solution:
The sentence presents a contrast between difficulties and the subject's continued efforts, suggesting admirable determination. The blank needs an adjective describing consistent, unwavering effort.

The correct option is "persistent", which means continuing firmly in a course of action despite difficulty.

The other options do not fit:

"Indifferent" means lacking interest, which contradicts the subject's dedication.

"Negligent" implies carelessness.

"Temporary" is about duration, not determination.

Thus, the correct sentence is: "Despite facing repeated setbacks in her research, Dr. Mehra remained persistent in her pursuit of a breakthrough."

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. We will obey your order and __________.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

We will obey your order and __________.
questions.solution:
According to the rule- if else is used with anybody/ nobody, etc. apostrophe ('s) will be used with else. So, 'nobody else's' is the correct fit for the given blank to convey the meaning of order of others.

Hence, option (b) is the suitable answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The project was completed __________ the initial deadline and so the manager was happy.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The project was completed __________ the initial deadline and so the manager was happy.
questions.solution:
Among the options, 'before' is the most appropriate word for the blank because the sentence states that the manager was happy due to the fact that the project was completed at a faster pace. This context cannot be achieved if 'later than' is used in the sentence.

'After than' is an incorrect phrase and the word 'earlier' requires 'than' to be complete. So, these options are negated.

The complete sentence is: "The project was completed before the initial deadline and so the manager was happy."

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Lambaste
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Lambaste
questions.solution:
Lambaste: To criticize (someone or something) harshly.

Censure: To express severe disapproval of (someone or something), typically in a formal statement.

Praise: To express approval or admiration of.

Applaud: To show approval or praise, especially by clapping.

Exonerate: To officially absolve (someone) from blame for a fault or wrongdoing.

The closest synonym in meaning is "Censure" (also "berate," "chastise," or "castigate").

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A Pyrrhic victory
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A Pyrrhic victory

options.text: A victory that comes at a devastatingly high cost
options.html: A victory that comes at a devastatingly high cost

options.text: A victory achieved through dishonest means
options.html: A victory achieved through dishonest means

questions.solution:
This idiom describes a victory that is won at such a great cost to the victor that it is tantamount to a defeat.

For example: "The company won the legal battle, but the huge legal fees and damaged reputation made it a Pyrrhic victory."

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. Churlish
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Churlish
questions.solution:
Churlish means rude in a mean-spirited and surly way. For example, "It would be churlish to refuse her generous offer."

Courteous means polite, respectful, or considerate in manner. For example, "The staff at the hotel were very courteous and helpful." Being polite and respectful is the direct opposite of being rude and surly, making courteous the correct antonym.

The other options - Boorish, Surly, and Rude are all synonyms of churlish.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.
